report_title: [SYNTHETIC TEST] Forest Loss Investigation: Koyna Corridor Forest Loss
summary: Autonomous vision analysis identified a linear_corridor of 4.16 ha (+/- 0.72 ha) at coordinates 17.4133 N, 73.7147 E between 2023-02-14 and 2023-05-25. Investigation mode: offline_simulated. Public records research linked the event to Linear Transportation / Road Infrastructure Expansion. Investigation status: concluded_with_evidence.
detailed_findings: OpenCV 5 classical computer vision detected a significant forest loss candidate covering 416 raster pixels (4.16 ha). The candidate region exhibited a major-to-minor aspect ratio of 9.66 and a compactness of 0.253. Investigation of public registries retrieved 6 records (Execution: offline_simulated). Estimated tree impact ranges from 998 to 1872 trees, based on Forest Survey of India (FSI) National Forest Inventory & Regional Working Plan Inventories (trees >= 10 cm DBH).

likely_causes_hypotheses.supporting_evidence: Visual linear geometry (Aspect Ratio > 3.0) strongly indicates corridor development. Public records searches in the Koyna sanctuary buffer reflect periodic road repair and diversion scrutiny, though specific statutory clearances must be confirmed via live Parivesh queries.

linked_entities_or_projects.entity_name: Public Works Department (PWD) / Regional Road Authority
linked_entities_or_projects.role: Subject to formal verification in state clearance gazettes.

conflicting_accounts: Environmental groups frequently raise concerns regarding tree felling along Koyna sanctuary buffer roads, while local administration maintains the necessity of village connectivity and emergency access.
unresolved_questions_and_unknowns: Specific contractor identities and exact tree felling permissions for this segment remain unverified.

tree_count_estimate.forest_type: Western Ghats Southern Moist Mixed Deciduous Forest (Champion & Seth Class 3B/C2)
tree_count_estimate.density_source: Forest Survey of India (FSI) National Forest Inventory & Regional Working Plan Inventories (trees >= 10 cm DBH)
tree_count_estimate.calculation_basis: Calculated from measured area (4.16 ha) multiplied by documented density range (240 - 450 stems/ha with DBH >= 10 cm) from Forest Survey of India (FSI) National Forest Inventory & Regional Working Plan Inventories (trees >= 10 cm DBH).
tree_count_estimate.limitations: Estimate reflects potential stems (DBH >= 10 cm) based on published stratified regional inventories. Does not reflect local slope variations, rock outcrops, or selective harvesting.
